newsitem.title: CHINA: HK stock market in danger of "Wild West" tag -SFC.
newsitem.headline: HK stock market in danger of "Wild West" tag -SFC.

text.p: Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) said the local stock market was running the risk of being labelled the "Wild West of the East" due to sharp swings in some stocks caused by investor speculation.

"The Hong Kong market is in danger of being regarded as the 'Wild West of the East' by the international financial press, because a small number of players are intent on breaking the rules," SFC chairman Anthony Neoh told the Chief Financial Officers Group of the Hong Kong Society of Accountants on Friday.

"This has produced the immediate result of a highly speculative market in more than a few shares. If share prices can rise substantially in one day, there is a tendency for investors to take an extremely short-term view and indeed we see signs of substantial day trading."
Neoh said that as investment horizons grow shorter, firms with longer term plans will find it difficult to raise capital.
"Markets driven by short-termism are prone to rumours and exploitation by insider traders and market manipulators," he said.
Neoh stressed the importance of good corporate governance, which should be accompanied by improved communications.
"Companies who allow rumours to cloud their businesses will not find it easy in the long run to attract capital," he said.
Neoh encouraged companies to look at where they could improve the content, timeliness and availability of company announcements.

"Companies which are always upfront in their disclosure of price-sensitive information will gain the respect of investors and the market and thereby hold the ability of tapping a larger pool of capital," he said.
